key_insight: In this PANS cohort, pain and fatigue were common, and higher symptom burden at presentation predicted later progression toward fibromyalgia criteria.
clinical_relevance: Early recognition of pain, fatigue, and other fibromyalgia-like symptoms in children with PANS may help identify those at higher risk for persistent symptom trajectories.
method: Prospective observational cohort of 204 consecutive PANS patients at a Stanford clinic
Used the 2016 ACR Fibromyalgia Survey Questionnaire, including WPI and SSS
Applied Cox proportional hazards modeling to assess predictors of progression
evidence_signal: Among 204 patients, 42% met fibromyalgia threshold scores at least once during follow-up and 13.7% progressed to full ACR fibromyalgia criteria, with higher WPI and SSS at presentation linked to greater hazard.
watch_item: Single-center observational data cannot prove causation, and results may not generalize beyond a specialty clinic population.
paper_title: Prevalence and Predictors of Pain and Fatigue in Pediatric Acute-Onset Neuropsychiatric Syndrome (PANS)
